propositions: Cancelled ACLI link-delete commands (due to missing --yes flag with stdin=DEVNULL) are miscounted as applied links because the CalledProcessError handler increments links_applied without discriminating idempotent failures from genuine cancellations.

The except CalledProcessError arm in _update_one_dispatch_links lacks output logging, making cancellations invisible except for upstream ACLI stderr traces, causing batch_outcome to report error=None with fabricated links_applied counts.

The silent-noop canary REBAR_RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP cannot detect this class of divergence because its check (computed>0 and applied==0) is defeated when applied is artificially inflated to equal computed.

The root cause is deterministic: acli 1.3.19-stable prompts for confirmation on link create and link delete without --yes, and with stdin=DEVNULL the prompt reads EOF, causing identical cancellation every pass.

The narrowed idempotent check must match both stderr and stdout for 404/409/does-not-exist/not-found markers, following the delete_issue precedent, to avoid false-positive failure counts on concurrent removal races.
Adding --yes to both link subcommands (mirroring the existing woritem delete pattern for bug 3256) removes the prompt that triggers cancellation.
